brief.title: Softmax: turning attention scores into weights
brief.objective: See what `att = F.softmax(att, dim=-1)` does in nanoGPT's manual attention path. Each row of scaled, masked scores becomes a row of non-negative weights that sum to 1. Masked future positions (-inf) get weight 0, and the weights are then used in `att @ v`.
brief.audience_context: The learner is in the attention concept and looking at CausalSelfAttention.forward in nanoGPT (model.py:65-71). They asked what the softmax call on line 69 does.
brief.scope_note: Left out to fit 15 seconds: the inside of the flash path (`scaled_dot_product_attention`), why scores are scaled by 1/sqrt(head size), attention dropout, and the other softmax in GPT.generate (model.py:324), which turns logits into sampling probabilities.

evidence.excerpt:
# flash attention make GPU go brrrrr but support is only in PyTorch >= 2.0
        self.flash = hasattr(torch.nn.functional, 'scaled_dot_product_attention')

# causal mask to ensure that attention is only applied to the left in the input sequence
            self.register_buffer("bias", torch.tril(torch.ones(config.block_size, config.block_size))
                                        .view(1, 1, config.block_size, config.block_size))

else:
            # manual implementation of attention
            att = (q @ k.transpose(-2, -1)) * (1.0 / math.sqrt(k.size(-1)))
            att = att.masked_fill(self.bias[:,:,:T,:T] == 0, float('-inf'))
            att = F.softmax(att, dim=-1)
            att = self.attn_dropout(att)
            y = att @ v # (B, nh, T, T) x (B, nh, T, hs) -> (B, nh, T, hs)

branches.runs: model.py:62-64: y = torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, attn_mask=None, dropout_p=self.dropout if self.training else 0, is_causal=True)

claim_registry.text: On the branch where `self.flash` is false (the manual implementation of attention), softmax is applied as `att = F.softmax(att, dim=-1)`, so it normalizes along the last dimension of `att`: each query's row of scores over key positions.

On the `self.flash` false branch, the order is: scores `(q @ k.transpose(-2, -1)) * (1.0 / math.sqrt(k.size(-1)))`, then `masked_fill(... == 0, float('-inf'))`, then `F.softmax(att, dim=-1)`, then `self.attn_dropout(att)`, then `y = att @ v`.

On the `self.flash` false branch, softmax turns each row of scores into non-negative weights that sum to 1. The positions the causal mask set to `float('-inf')` (future positions) get weight 0, so attention goes only to the left in the sequence.
When `self.flash` is true, this explicit softmax line does not run. Attention is computed by `torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, ..., is_causal=True)` instead.

must_show: The code line `att = F.softmax(att, dim=-1)`, marked as part of the `else` branch (taken when `self.flash` is false)
One row of attention scores in which the future positions hold -inf after `masked_fill`
That row turning into weights: larger scores get larger weights, -inf entries become exactly 0
The resulting row of weights summing to 1, with the row's length unchanged
The arrow showing softmax works across the last dimension (along a row, over key positions)
The weights then flowing into `y = att @ v`
must_not_claim: That `F.softmax` always runs, or runs on every forward pass. It runs only when `self.flash` is false.
That softmax is applied before the causal mask, or that masking happens after softmax
That softmax comes after `att @ v` or after dropout. The order is scores, mask, softmax, dropout, `att @ v`.
That softmax picks only the single largest score (argmax) and zeroes all the others
That softmax removes masked positions or changes the shape of `att`. It keeps the T×T shape, and masked entries become 0.
That softmax normalizes down columns or across the whole matrix instead of along `dim=-1` (each row)
That the flash path skips causal masking or gives different semantics. That path uses `is_causal=True`.
brief.visual_direction: Start on the highlighted `else` branch line `att = F.softmax(att, dim=-1)`, then move attention to a single row of scores. The -inf cells sit at the right, marked as future tokens. Show the transformation: each score grows into a bar whose size reflects its weight, the -inf cells collapse to zero, and the bars together fill exactly one whole unit. Mark the direction of normalization along the row. End with the row of weights flowing into `att @ v`, keeping the sequence mask → softmax → `att @ v` visible as a short chain so cause and order are clear.

findings.description: Blank or near-blank frames: #0 (0.00 s, luma stddev 1.34), #1 (0.03 s, luma stddev 1.35). Every sampled frame (0, 1, each beat's start, start + 1, middle and end - 1, and the last frame) needs luma standard deviation above 2; the final render is refused otherwise.

The small weights chart inside the `y = att @ v` box has tiny value labels (0.61, 0.12, 0.27) and a tiny 'weights' tag that are still too small to read at full size. The bar shapes still make it clear that these are the weights.

While 'sum = 1' is shown, the 'dim=-1: along the row, over key positions' arrow and its label fade to dark brown on the dark background. This low contrast makes the required direction-of-normalization marker hard to pick out, though it can still be read.
The side note 'If true: scaled_dot_product_attention, is_causal=True' is small, thin, grey italic text on the dark background. Its contrast is low next to the main code lines.
The opening frame shows only a very faint 'if self.flash:' on an otherwise empty screen, so the video starts almost empty before the highlighted softmax line appears.

The shrunken weights row that flows into the `y = att @ v` box keeps its value labels (0.61, 0.12, 0.27) and 'weights' tag. At this scale they are only a few pixels tall, so even at full size they are specks a learner cannot read. The bar shapes still carry the idea.
